reason: The text describes the suffering of the Israelites under Egyptian taskmasters (nogashim) who oppress them. God explicitly acknowledges hearing the cry of His people 'because of their oppressors' (מִפְּנֵי נֹגְשָׂיו) and recognizes their affliction (עֳנִי עַמִּי). While the passage frames this within God's redemptive response rather than as political analysis, it does portray those in power (Egyptian authorities) inflicting suffering on subjugated people (Hebrew slaves), which substantiates the statement's core claim, even if expressed in modern terminology.
